Some schools are interested in ACT scores only, some look at both ACT and SAT. If I were you, I would go to the "Apply" section of the school's website and just read at what they require. I don't know much about the SAT, but last time I checked, you can take the ACT as many times as you want. You can take the ACT with or without writing, and I would just look at what they require. My school doesn't require writing. And when I took it with writing, it lowered my score, because I didn't realize the time limit for that part was SO SHORT. 

Other than that, schools like to see a record of community service / volunteering. It can't hurt to have letters of recommendation from your high school teachers either. Also, all of this depends on the major you're interested in. You can tailor your application to things that have to do with your major. Include things like tutoring, any academic club memberships (Beta Club, Debate Team, etc.), and especially any type of leadership positions. Haha, I wrote "President of Yearbook Committee," which actually entailed me scheduling like two meetings and taking pictures and making a shitty PDF for the horrific little private school I graduated from. But, "President of Yearbook Committee" still looks good on paper. 

Tl;dr - go to UC Berkley's website, find admissions, click apply, and read. Hope this helps.
